title: How to Register for BIR Business Registration (Form 1901)
description: Official tax registration for sole proprietors, freelancers, and self-employed professionals.

blocks.content: BIR Business Registration using BIR Form 1901 is the process of registering a sole proprietorship business, self-employed individual, freelancer, or mixed-income earner with the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR).
After registration, the taxpayer receives a Certificate of Registration (COR), authority to issue receipts or invoices, and official tax obligations under Philippine tax laws.

The BIR Business Registration is commonly used for:
* Legal business operations
* Tax compliance and filing
* Issuing official receipts or invoices
* Opening business bank accounts

You may need BIR Business Registration using Form 1901 if you are:
- A sole proprietor with DTI registration
- A freelancer or self-employed professional
- An online seller or content creator
- A mixed-income earner with business income
- Starting a small business or consultancy

content.title: Benefits of Having BIR Business Registration

blocks.title: Legal Tax Compliance
blocks.content: Registration ensures compliance with Philippine tax laws and regulations.

blocks.title: Authority to Issue Receipts or Invoices
blocks.content: Registered businesses may legally issue official receipts or invoices to customers and clients.

blocks.title: Required for Business Transactions
blocks.content: Banks, suppliers, government agencies, and clients often require BIR registration documents.
Applicants may process BIR registration through online systems or physical Revenue District Offices (RDOs).

blocks.title: Online Application
blocks.content:
Some taxpayers may register through:
* BIR Online Registration and Update System (ORUS)
* Electronic submission channels
Availability may depend on taxpayer classification and RDO support.

blocks.title: Walk-In Application
blocks.content: Applicants may visit the Revenue District Office (RDO) with jurisdiction over the business address.
Personal appearance may be required for verification and registration.
**Pro Tip:** Use the BIR **eFPS or eBIRForms** for faster filing and avoid manual queuing at the RDO. Most payments can now be done via GCash or Maya.

blocks.title: Prepare Your Business Documents
blocks.content:
Prepare your:
* DTI registration
* Mayor's Permit or proof of application
* Valid IDs
* Proof of address
* Completed BIR Form 1901

blocks.title: Submit BIR Form 1901
blocks.content: Submit the accomplished form and requirements to your assigned RDO.
The officer will verify your taxpayer classification and registration details.

blocks.title: Pay the Registration Fees
blocks.content:
Depending on current BIR policies and taxpayer type, fees may include:
* Documentary Stamp Tax
* Loose-leaf or invoicing fees
* Other applicable charges

Payments may be made through:
* Authorized Agent Banks
* ePayment systems
* Online payment channels

blocks.title: Register Books of Accounts
blocks.content:
Businesses are generally required to register:
* Manual books
* Loose-leaf books
* Computerized books of accounts
The BIR may stamp or electronically acknowledge the books.

blocks.title: Apply for Official Receipts or Invoices
blocks.content:
Businesses must secure:
* Authority to Print (ATP), or
* BIR-approved invoicing system
This allows legal issuance of invoices or receipts.

blocks.title: Claim the Certificate of Registration (COR)
blocks.content:
After approval, the BIR issues:
* BIR Form 2303 (Certificate of Registration)
* Official tax type details
* “Ask for Receipt” notice
* Registered books information
Display the COR at your business establishment.

Applicants may process BIR Business Registration at:
- Bureau of Internal Revenue Revenue District Office (RDO)
- BIR Online Registration and Update System (ORUS)
- Authorized Agent Banks (for payments)
Applications are generally filed with the RDO having jurisdiction over the business address.

Typical processing timelines include:
* Basic registration approval: Same day to 3 business days
* Books of accounts registration: Same day
* Official receipt/invoice printing: 1–2 weeks
* Online applications: Depends on RDO processing

Applicants may monitor their application through:
* BIR ORUS portal
* RDO inquiry counters
* Email notifications
* Accredited printer updates
If you applied through ORUS, keep a record of your Transaction Reference Number (TRN) to easily track the progress of your application online.

Applicants may experience:
- Incorrect RDO assignment
- Incomplete documentary requirements
- Delays in receipt printing
- Missing permit requirements
- Incorrect taxpayer classification

items: Verify your assigned RDO before applying
Prepare both printed and digital copies of requirements
Keep multiple copies of your COR and receipts

blocks.content: For the most reliable information on tax registration and business compliance, please refer to the official BIR channels:

items: **Online Portal:** [BIR ORUS (Online Registration and Update System)](https://orus.bir.gov.ph)
**Inquiries:** You may also visit your assigned Revenue District Office (RDO) for direct assistance.

blocks.title: Who should use BIR Form 1901?
blocks.content: BIR Form 1901 is commonly used by sole proprietors, freelancers, professionals, and self-employed individuals.

blocks.title: Is the ₱500 annual registration fee still required?
blocks.content: BIR policies may change over time. Verify the latest fee requirements directly with the BIR.

blocks.title: Do freelancers need BIR registration?
blocks.content: Yes. Freelancers and self-employed professionals generally need BIR registration for legal tax compliance.

blocks.title: Can I register online?
blocks.content: Some registrations may be processed through BIR ORUS depending on eligibility and RDO support.

blocks.title: What is BIR Form 2303?
blocks.content: BIR Form 2303 is the Certificate of Registration (COR) issued after successful business registration.
